tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

---
name: job-search-inbox-sweep-method
description: How to sweep Devin's Gmail for in-flight interviews without missing companies — never filter out recruiting-system senders, and always check starred mail.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When Devin asks for his list of in-flight companies ("update my matrix"), missing a company is the failure he cares most about. It has happened four times (SpaceX, Render, Expedia, Robinhood on 2026-10-01).

**Why:** The Robinhood miss came from a "human senders only" Gmail query that excluded `notifications@`, `no-reply@`, Ashby, Greenhouse and similar senders. Recruiter outreach and scheduling mail is sent through exactly those systems (e.g. `notifications@recruiting.robinhood.com`, `notifications@guide.klaviyo.com`, Calendly, GoodTime, candidate.fyi, HackerRank). Following only the first page of results also dropped mail.

**How to apply:** Run all of these and read every page:
1. Recruiting-system senders: ashbyhq, greenhouse, lever, myworkday, icims, smartrecruiters, gem, goodtime, modernloop, candidate.fyi, guide.co, calendly, brighthire, hackerrank, codesignal.
2. Subject keywords: invitation, interview, phone screen, next steps, availability, assessment, schedule, recruiter, "let's chat", connect.
3. `is:starred` — Devin stars the recruiter emails he cares about.
4. Sent mail, to see what he has already answered.
For oversized results, list sender/subject/date with jq from the saved file instead of skipping. Report the list without tiers; he wants one flat list. See [[job-search-targeting-criteria]].

StubHub, Senior Software Engineer - Supply Core (Fullstack). Recruiter Joseph Gordon, coordinator Ida Badri.

- Code pair: 2026-10-08 2:30-4:00pm EDT (75 min + buffer), Chongshu Qian + Ali Rehman. Languages allowed: C#, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python3. Recruiter email: one problem in parts, OOP, data objects, date-time library, "no brute force".
- System design: 2026-10-09 2:30-3:30pm EDT, Tianxu Zhang + Richard Fornario, on Excalidraw.

Public reports (Blind, LeetCode discuss 5223346, prachub, linkjob; 2024-2026) are unusually consistent:
- Code pair = "marketing engine": Customer/Event classes, `send_customer_notifications`; parts: same-city events → event closest to next birthday → 5 nearest by distance → 5 cheapest via a slow/flaky price API → make campaigns composable (Strategy). 5-6 parts; finishing all parts matters.
- System design = marketing/event email notification system ("1M emails in 5 minutes", or 1M events emailing registrants). One variant: internal chat + 10-day-inactivity re-engagement emails. Not "design Ticketmaster".

The prep PDF attachment (`StubHub_Interview_Prep_-_SIM_-_BE_(1).pdf`) could not be read by the Gmail connector (no attachment download; browsers not signed in) as of 2026-10-07.

Related: [[system-design-interview-weak-spot]], [[email-service-deep-dive-project]] (the SNS→SQS story maps directly onto the email-system prompt).

2026-10-07: on the prep call, recruiter Joseph Gordon told Devin the coding problem is "related to email notification" — consistent with the marketing-engine question. Devin did a full Python mock of Q1-Q5 the same day; recurring slips were not running code before submitting, the `bisect_left` off-by-one (before is `index - 1`), and skipping clarifying questions.

*About the Role:*
We are seeking an experienced Back-End engineer to be part of our Identity
product group. In this role, you will be part of the cloud product software
engineering team, responsible for developing new features and working
closely with other teams such as UI and Sensor. This is a hybrid role and
will requires the ability to work 2 days per week from our offices in
Sunnyvale CA.,

*What You'll Do:*

The right candidate will possess proven software engineering skills, with
experience building and launching large, distributed systems in a
team-centric environment. You will work and contribute to a dynamic,
entrepreneurial setting and will mentor junior engineers.

In this role, you must be comfortable managing competing priorities and be
able to bring order to ambiguous scenarios. Maturity, impeccable judgment,
and the ability to influence and lead are essential to success in this
role.

Candidates must be data-driven and analytical. You will be required to
clearly & effectively communicate (written as well as verbally) across the
organization and up to senior leadership. Our team members must have a
growth mindset.

*What You’ll Need:*

   -

   9+ years of professional software development experience
   -

   5+ years of programming experience with at least one modern language
   such as Go, Java, C++, or C# including object-oriented design
   -

   4+ years of experience contributing to the architecture and design
   (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current
   systems
   -

   Experience building cloud-deployed applications
   -

   BS/BE in CS or related field
   -

   Ability to work well with a group of senior engineers in a dynamic, fast
   paced environment.

Alice Lobos,

Nubank

Devin,

Thank you for your interest in opportunities at Gusto! We appreciate the time and effort you’ve invested in applying to our open positions.

Our records indicate that you have submitted multiple applications within the past 30 days. To ensure a fair and efficient hiring process, we kindly ask candidates to limit applications to no more than five roles within a 30-day period. This allows us to focus on evaluating each application thoroughly and fairly.

At this time, we are unable to process additional applications from you within this window. However, your active applications are still being reviewed, and our team will reach out with updates as soon as we have news to share.

If you feel strongly about a specific role, we encourage you to prioritize applying for those positions that best align with your skills, experience, and career aspirations.

Thank you for your understanding and continued interest in Gusto!

Warm regards,

Gusto’s Invite Team

lastPrompt: Can you update my list of companies and tell me what is pending on my side

content.text:
Swept everything through this evening (Wed Oct 7). Two things changed the shape of the list: **Gusto is new**, and **CoreWeave, Nubank, Zipline and Cloudflare Deploy at Scale all advanced today** and are each waiting on you.

## Pending on your side

1. **Zipline — reply to Dora with afternoon availability for next week.** She got the go-ahead to run the interviews virtually and has now asked twice for afternoon ET slots; you've only sent mornings.
2. **Cloudflare, Deploy at Scale — three items.** You passed the coding round and are invited to the team interviews:
   - Submit availability through the "Find A Time" link (they want 2–4 hours a day across the next 5 business days).
   - Sign the NDA.
   - Fill in the export-controls questionnaire.
3. **CoreWeave — submit availability in the candidate portal.** You passed the recruiter screen; they want at least two weeks of availability.
4. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14.** Design a solution for their "Purple Journey" platform, as a document or up to 10 slides, emailed to Alice Lobos. A 1.5-hour presentation follows; she'll send slots. I can't open the attached PDF brief.
5. **Tesla — accept the calendar invite** for Oct 15 if you haven't; Zette asked for an explicit accept.

I can't see form submissions or calendar responses, so items 2, 3 and 5 may already be done.

**Conflicts to avoid when you send Zipline and Cloudflare times:**
- Mon Oct 12 is gone entirely (Aurora, Pittsburgh).
- The Wed Oct 14 12:30–3:00 window you gave Intuit now overlaps Gusto at 1:00. If Intuit picks that day, one has to move.
- The Thu Oct 15 12:30–2:00 Intuit window runs right up to Tesla at 2:00.

## Everything in flight (19)

All times ET.

| Company | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Robinhood | Senior SWE, Enterprise Build | Architecture interview with Zhe Sun, **Thu Oct 8 10:30–11:30am** |
| StubHub | Senior SWE, Supply Core | Code pair **Thu Oct 8 2:30–4:00pm**; system design **Fri Oct 9 2:30–3:30pm** |
| Duolingo | Backend Engineer | Recruiter chat with Jenn Nguyen, **Fri Oct 9 10:20–10:40am** (booked) |
| Render | Software Engineer, Product | Technical screen **Fri Oct 9 1:00–2:00pm** |
| Aurora | Senior SWE, Full Stack | Onsite in Pittsburgh **Mon Oct 12 10:15am–5:00pm**; flights and hotel confirmed |
| Klaviyo | Senior SWE, Platform Engineering | Hiring manager screen with Kevin Flathers, **Tue Oct 13 10:00–11:00am** |
| Rivian | Staff SWE | Recruiter screen **Tue Oct 13 1:30–2:00pm** |
| Gusto (new) | Staff SWE, Financial Platform | Recruiter screen with Khetsun Tenzin, **Wed Oct 14 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Nubank | Staff SWE | Case study due **Wed Oct 14**, then presentation |
| Tesla | Distributed Systems Engineer, Fintech | CoderPad interview with Shiv Thakur, **Thu Oct 15 2:00–2:45pm** |
| Stripe | Backend Engineer, Data & AI | Recruiter call with Pilar Wilsie, **Thu Oct 15 4:15–4:45pm** |
| Riot Games | — | Phone screen **Tue Oct 27 3:00–3:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews: you owe availability, NDA and questionnaire |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Technical done today; awaiting result |
| Zipline | — | Virtual loop approved; you owe afternoon availability |
| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Passed recruiter screen; you owe availability |
| Intuit | Staff level | Final round; afternoon windows for Oct 13–16 sent to Shelby, awaiting a time |

structuredContent.plaintextBody:
Hi Devin,

Thank you for taking the time to apply for the Staff Software Engineer, Robinhood Command Center position. We've been extremely fortunate to have a fantastic response from accomplished candidates such as yourself for this role. However, after careful consideration, we've made the decision to not move forward with the interview process at this time. We really appreciate your time and efforts in applying. We’d love to stay in touch as our team continues to grow and reconnect down the line.

Thanks again for your interest in Robinhood, and we wish you the best of luck in your search!

Kind regards,
Robinhood Recruiting Team

content.text:
Updated through this evening (Thu Oct 8). **Affirm is new**, and Zipline, CoreWeave and both Cloudflare roles all moved; the list is now 20 companies.

## Pending on your side

1. **Cloudflare, Internal Fraud Platform — you passed the technical.** Three items, all sent fresh today by Adam Asad for this role:
   - Submit availability through the "Find A Time" link (2–4 hours a day over the next 5 business days).
   - Sign the NDA.
   - Fill in the export-controls questionnaire.
2. **Affirm — book the recruiter call.** Amanda Ballesteros sent a scheduling link for a 30-minute call about Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning). She is out until the week of Oct 19, so it has to land then.
3. **CoreWeave — reply to confirm** the Fri Oct 16 interview; the confirmation email asks for it.
4. **Cloudflare, Deploy at Scale — reply to confirm** the Oct 20 and Oct 22 interviews; same ask.
5. **Intuit — withdraw the Wed Oct 14 window.** You offered Shelby 12:30–3:00 that day, and it is now fully taken by Gusto at 1:00 and Zipline from 1:30. Your other three windows are still clear.
6. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14.** That day is already Gusto plus a 3.5-hour Zipline loop, and Monday is Aurora, so realistically it needs to be done over the weekend or Tuesday.
7. **Zipline — prepare the 45-minute panel presentation** for Wednesday (most challenging project, with architecture diagrams).
8. **Tesla — accept the calendar invite** for Oct 15 if you haven't.

I can't see form submissions or calendar responses, so parts of 1 and 8 may already be done.

## Everything in flight (20)

All times ET.

| Company | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Duolingo | Backend Engineer | Recruiter chat **Fri Oct 9 10:20–10:40am** |
| Render | Software Engineer, Product | Technical screen **Fri Oct 9 1:00–2:00pm** |
| StubHub | Senior SWE, Supply Core | Code pair was today; system design **Fri Oct 9 2:30–3:30pm** |
| Aurora | Senior SWE, Full Stack | Onsite in Pittsburgh **Mon Oct 12 10:15am–5:00pm** |
| Klaviyo | Senior SWE, Platform Engineering | Hiring manager screen **Tue Oct 13 10:00–11:00am** |
| Zipline | Senior SWE, ASW Launch Ops | Prep call with Dora **Tue Oct 13 12:30–1:00pm**; virtual onsite **Wed Oct 14 1:30–5:00pm** |
| Rivian | Staff SWE | Recruiter screen **Tue Oct 13 1:30–2:00pm** |
| Gusto | Staff SWE, Financial Platform | Recruiter screen **Wed Oct 14 1:00–1:30pm** (ends as Zipline starts) |
| Nubank | Staff SWE | Case study due **Wed Oct 14**, then a 1.5-hour presentation |
| Tesla | Distributed Systems Engineer, Fintech | CoderPad interview **Thu Oct 15 2:00–2:45pm** |
| Stripe | Backend Engineer, Data & AI | Recruiter call **Thu Oct 15 4:15–4:45pm** |
| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Interview with Max Odenheimer (Engineering Manager) **Fri Oct 16 4:30–5:15pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews **Tue Oct 20 2:00–5:00pm** and **Thu Oct 22 3:45–5:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Advanced to team interviews; you owe availability and forms |
| Affirm (new) | Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning) | Recruiter call to be booked, week of Oct 19 |
| Riot Games | — | Phone screen **Tue Oct 27 3:00–3:30pm** |
| Robinhood | Senior SWE, Enterprise Build | Architecture interview was today; awaiting result |
| Intuit | Staff level | Final round; awaiting a time from Shelby |
| CrowdStrike | Back-end engineer, Identity | Andy is setting something up with Prathima; awaiting |
| BrightHire | AI engineering | No reply from Will Decker since your Oct 6 note |

Long shot: **Chime** — Alex replied today that he has been circulating your profile to partner recruiters and nobody has picked it up so far.

## Also in the mail

- **Robinhood** rejected a separate application (Staff SWE, Command Center). That is not the Enterprise Build role you interviewed for today.
- Application-stage rejections with no process attached: Uber, Reddit, Docker, Toast, Grafana, Microsoft, AMD, and two DoorDash roles closed.

Gusto and Affirm aren't on your jobwatch skip list yet; say the word and I'll add them.

Robinhood Recruiting Team

structuredContent.plaintextBody:
Hi Devin,

Thanks for taking the time to speak with me earlier today! We are excited to start the interview process for the Senior/Software Engineer II, Backend role.

As we discussed, the first step in the official interview process is the Technical Video Interview with one of our Software Engineers.

The interview will take around 60 minutes, please provide your preferred coding language from the following:

• Swift/Kotlin

• Python

• Java

• Javascript

This will be a live coding session that will cover fundamental coding skills, data structures, and algorithms.

Please let us know some dates and times that work best for you over the next week using the link at the bottom of this email.

I've copied Julie on this email. She is our Talent Coordinator who will be handling all the scheduling throughout the process.

Best,

Jenn

**Jennifer Nguyen is asking to see your availability**

Let Jennifer know when you're free to meet. This will help them find the best time for your upcoming interviews.

[Share your availability](http://url9288.recruiting.duolingo.com/ls/click?upn=u001.jC3Fg1I68tzaX-2ByUbk4M82KONe-2FBRb8fiG93AbOGAtYswB8kIkHCDLuqf2L2-2Fv-2BrwCkwYyXGLICSszEyQ8KYo6TrmeEHkufN-2BCx5Fi9v0InR4CNqq4P5zOCJgVRcZNyFrbHl2GJL9CjFty7Gi77sat110uhV1xsr2-2FrluPh03qBXqVKfH28LXZqhme8a9M9NNuQoMg5stc61x7lvIGuzo2YFitBU1H19YGin1DeJb6nVuzce7rDkazs3d-2BZpsAnTNrq3_EyqcVURF02Ai3MPxiHDVog6mqmr3NUJ2gXqr1CzotrNJ7xoEJbT0-2BbgbtMQHNKsL3u0wf9SjtW9hDjhEFkC1ATP5qQyOF6-2Ba03e66GdM4y2-2FymoiBHv1eFT0WE0uvjG4jW55NKBQKbqvRKmZxsBfJ54yuVk2Aba9-2BYE2QTwm8KkCic476zFO7BaDJ0A6oI2qEpqW-2FZVmZLhAWIvSxLJ1xw-3D-3D

content.text:
Updated through Sunday evening (Oct 11). Nothing new entered or dropped out, so it's still 20 companies; the changes are Duolingo advancing, Cloudflare Fraud getting scheduled, and Aurora's schedule shifting for tomorrow.

**For tomorrow:** Aurora now starts at **11:15am**, not 10:15. They pulled the system design round because of an interviewer conflict and will reschedule it virtually. Your RIC–PHL flight has been repeatedly delayed today and American rebooked your connection, so check the new arrival time.

## Pending on your side

1. **Duolingo — send availability and pick a language.** You passed the recruiter chat; next is a 60-minute live coding interview. Jenn wants times over the next week through the portal link, plus your choice of Python, Java, JavaScript or Swift/Kotlin.
2. **Affirm — book the recruiter call** for the week of Oct 19. I see no booking confirmation yet.
3. **Intuit — withdraw the Wed Oct 14 window and nudge.** That window is now taken by Gusto and Zipline, and Shelby has been silent since you sent times on Oct 6.
4. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14**, emailed to Alice Lobos.
5. **Zipline — panel presentation** ready for Wednesday; prep call with Dora is Tuesday.
6. **CoreWeave and Cloudflare Deploy at Scale — reply to confirm.** Both confirmation emails asked for a reply and I see none in your sent mail.

I can't see portal submissions, so 1 and 2 may already be done.

## Everything in flight (20)

All times ET.

| Company | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Aurora | Senior SWE, Full Stack | Onsite in Pittsburgh **Mon Oct 12 11:15am–5:00pm**; system design to follow virtually |
| Klaviyo | Senior SWE, Platform Engineering | Hiring manager screen **Tue Oct 13 10:00–11:00am** |
| Zipline | Senior SWE, ASW Launch Ops | Prep call **Tue Oct 13 12:30–1:00pm**; virtual onsite **Wed Oct 14 1:30–5:00pm** |
| Rivian | Staff SWE | Recruiter screen **Tue Oct 13 1:30–2:00pm** |
| Gusto | Staff SWE, Financial Platform | Recruiter screen **Wed Oct 14 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Nubank | Staff SWE | Case study due **Wed Oct 14**, then presentation |
| Tesla | Distributed Systems Engineer, Fintech | CoderPad interview **Thu Oct 15 2:00–2:45pm** |
| Stripe | Backend Engineer, Data & AI | Recruiter call **Thu Oct 15 4:15–4:45pm** |
| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Interview with the engineering manager **Fri Oct 16 4:30–5:15pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews **Tue Oct 20 2:00–5:00pm** and **Thu Oct 22 3:45–5:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Team interviews **Thu Oct 22 9:00am–12:15pm** (coding, design, cross-functional, values) |
| Riot Games | — | Phone screen **Tue Oct 27 3:00–3:30pm** |
| Duolingo | Senior/SWE II, Backend | Passed recruiter chat; technical interview to be scheduled |
| Affirm | Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning) | Recruiter call to be booked, week of Oct 19 |
| Intuit | Staff level | Final round; no time yet from Shelby |
| StubHub | Senior SWE, Supply Core | Code pair and system design both done; awaiting result |
| Render | Software Engineer, Product | Technical screen done Oct 9; awaiting result |
| Robinhood | Senior SWE, Enterprise Build | Architecture interview done Oct 8; awaiting result |
| CrowdStrike | Back-end engineer, Identity | Andy was setting up a conversation on Oct 7; nothing since |
| BrightHire | AI engineering | No reply from Will Decker since Oct 6 |

Long shot: **Chime** — nothing since Alex's Oct 8 note.

## Also in the mail

- **Thu Oct 22 is now a double Cloudflare day:** Fraud Platform in the morning, Deploy at Scale in the afternoon.
- **Robinhood** sent a rejection on Oct 9 for "Senior Software Engineer, Backend". By title that is a separate application, not Enterprise Build, but it uses the same wording as a post-interview decline, so I can't rule out that it is the result of Thursday's interview.
- **CoreWeave** rejected a different application (Senior SWE, IAM). The Oct 16 interview is for Senior SWE I and has not been cancelled.
- **New outreach:** an agency recruiter pitched Symmetric Health, Senior SWE at $180K plus bonus. That is well under your bar.
- Application-stage rejections: Notion, NVIDIA, ServiceNow, Samsara, American Express, Uber (a second role); Hinge Health filled its role.

lastPrompt: is there anything I owe right now?

content.text:
Yes. Nothing new has come in since the last sweep, and you've sent no job-search email since Oct 7, so these are still open, in order of urgency:

1. **Duolingo — availability and coding language.** Jenn asked on Friday for times over the next week plus your language choice (Python, Java, JavaScript or Swift/Kotlin), through the portal link. This is the most overdue item.
2. **Intuit — withdraw the Wed Oct 14 12:30–3:00 window.** It now collides with Gusto at 1:00 and Zipline from 1:30, and Shelby could still book it. Worth sending tonight or first thing tomorrow.
3. **Affirm — book the recruiter call** for the week of Oct 19 using Amanda's scheduling link.
4. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14**, emailed to Alice Lobos. With Aurora tomorrow and Zipline on Wednesday, Tuesday is your only real working day for it.
5. **Zipline — the 45-minute panel presentation** for Wednesday 1:30pm.
6. **CoreWeave and Cloudflare Deploy at Scale — reply to confirm** the scheduled interviews. Both asked for a reply; low stakes, but it takes one line each.

For Duolingo and Affirm I'm inferring from the absence of a confirmation email, since I can't see portal or scheduling-link submissions. If you've already done either, cross it off.

You owe nothing to StubHub, Render, Robinhood, CrowdStrike, BrightHire or Chime; those are all waiting on them.

If it helps, I can draft the Intuit note and the two confirmation replies for you to send.

content.text:
Updated as of Sunday night (Oct 11). You cleared most of the list this evening; Affirm is now booked and nothing else changed status.

## What you cleared tonight

- **Affirm:** recruiter call booked for **Mon Oct 26 1:00–1:30pm** (Zoom audio).
- **Duolingo:** told Jenn your language is Python.
- **CoreWeave:** confirmed the Oct 16 interview.
- **Cloudflare, Internal Fraud Platform:** confirmed the Oct 22 interviews.
- **Intuit:** nudged Shelby for a tentative day.

## Still open on your side

1. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14**, emailed to Alice Lobos. Tuesday is your only real working day for it.
2. **Zipline — 45-minute panel presentation** for Wed Oct 14 at 1:30pm.
3. **Intuit — the Wed Oct 14 window is still on offer.** Your nudge didn't withdraw it, and it collides with Gusto at 1:00 and Zipline from 1:30. If Shelby replies with Wednesday, you'll need to decline it; a one-line follow-up now would prevent that.
4. **Duolingo — availability, if not already submitted.** Your email covered the language only. Jenn asked for times through the portal link, and I can't see whether you filled that in.
5. **Cloudflare, Deploy at Scale — reply to confirm** Oct 20 and Oct 22. You confirmed the Fraud Platform thread but not this one. Low stakes.

## Everything in flight (20)

All times ET.

|---|---|---|

| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Interview **Fri Oct 16 4:30–5:15pm** (confirmed) |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews **Tue Oct 20 2:00–5:00pm** and **Thu Oct 22 3:45–5:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Team interviews **Thu Oct 22 9:00am–12:15pm** (confirmed) |
| Affirm | Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning) | Recruiter call **Mon Oct 26 1:00–1:30pm** |

entries.description: Lists draft emails from the authenticated user's Gmail account, optionally filtered by a query string. Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of drafts to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. A token received from a previous `list_drafts` call to retrieve the next page of results. Leave empty to fetch the first page. This is primarily used for pagination to continue fetching results from where the previous `ListDraft` call left off, especially when the number of drafts matching the query exceeds the `page_size` limit.

query.description: Examples: - `subject:OneMCP Update` - `from:gduser1@workspacesamples.dev` - `to:gduser2@workspacesamples.dev AND newer_than:7d` - `project proposal has:attachment` - `is:unread` A space or a dash (`-`) will separate a number while a dot (`.`) will be a decimal. For example, `01.2047-100` is considered two numbers: `01.2047` and `100`. Note: If we want to ensure all drafts for the query are returned, we can paginate the results by making repeated calls to the tool until the response contains an empty list of drafts.

view.description: Optional. Controls the fields populated for drafts in the draft list. Defaults to returning metadata only (`id`, `thread_id`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`). Set to `DRAFT_VIEW_FULL` to include `subject` and `plaintext_body` content.

content.text:
Updated through Monday evening (Oct 12). **GitHub is new**, Duolingo is scheduled, and Aurora wants times for the make-up system design round. That makes 21 companies.

## On your side

1. **GitHub — pick an interview time and sign the NDA.** Kevin Lamsback moved you to the next stage for Staff Software Engineer, Git Systems. There's a scheduling link in his email and a separate NDA email; the NDA has to be done before the call.
2. **Aurora — send availability for the virtual system design interview.** Catherine asked this afternoon and wants it early this week.
3. **Nubank — case study due Wed Oct 14**, emailed to Alice Lobos.
4. **Zipline — 45-minute panel presentation** for Wed Oct 14 at 1:30pm.
5. **Hold Thu Oct 15 12:30–2:00pm and Fri Oct 16 1:15–2:30pm for Intuit** until Lakshmi confirms one, due by Tuesday midday Pacific.
6. **Audible hotel charge (not an interview item).** Jaramie replied that the hotel should never have charged you and that they couldn't get it moved to the company card; the email then tells you what to do next, most likely submit it for reimbursement. I only read the opening of that message, so check it for the exact steps.

**Watch Thursday when you give Aurora and GitHub times.** It already holds Duolingo coding at 10:30, a possible 75-minute Intuit final at 12:30, Tesla coding at 2:00 and Stripe at 4:15.

## Everything in flight (21)

All times ET.

| Company | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Klaviyo | Senior SWE, Platform Engineering | Hiring manager screen **Tue Oct 13 10:00–11:00am** |
| Zipline | Senior SWE, ASW Launch Ops | Prep call **Tue Oct 13 12:30–1:00pm**; virtual onsite **Wed Oct 14 1:30–5:00pm** |
| Rivian | Staff SWE | Recruiter screen **Tue Oct 13 1:30–2:00pm** |
| Gusto | Staff SWE, Financial Platform | Recruiter screen **Wed Oct 14 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Nubank | Staff SWE | Case study due **Wed Oct 14**, then presentation |
| Duolingo | Senior/SWE II, Backend | Technical video interview **Thu Oct 15 10:30–11:30am** |
| Intuit | Staff level | Final round **Thu Oct 15 or Fri Oct 16**, to be confirmed Tuesday |
| Tesla | Distributed Systems Engineer, Fintech | CoderPad interview **Thu Oct 15 2:00–2:45pm** |
| Stripe | Backend Engineer, Data & AI | Recruiter call **Thu Oct 15 4:15–4:45pm** |
| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Interview **Fri Oct 16 4:30–5:15pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews **Tue Oct 20 2:00–5:00pm** and **Thu Oct 22 3:45–5:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Team interviews **Thu Oct 22 9:00am–12:15pm** |
| Affirm | Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning) | Recruiter call **Mon Oct 26 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Riot Games | — | Phone screen **Tue Oct 27 3:00–3:30pm** |
| Aurora | Senior SWE, Full Stack | Onsite done today; virtual system design to be scheduled |
| GitHub (new) | Staff SWE, Git Systems | First conversation to be booked; NDA to sign |
| StubHub | Senior SWE, Supply Core | Both rounds done; awaiting result |
| Render | Software Engineer, Product | Technical screen done Oct 9; awaiting result |
| Robinhood | Senior SWE, Enterprise Build | Architecture interview done Oct 8; awaiting result |
| CrowdStrike | Back-end engineer, Identity | Nothing since Andy's Oct 7 note |
| BrightHire | AI engineering | No reply from Will Decker since Oct 6 |

Long shot: **Chime** — nothing since Oct 8.

## Also in the mail

- You sent about 18 new applications last night; all are acknowledgements only so far.
- Application-stage rejections today: Suno, Runway, Samsara (Maps Services), and another NVIDIA role.

Hi Devin,

The technical round went well, and we’d like to move you forward to the final stage of our process!

For the final interview round, there will be three 45 minute behavioral interviews.

1. Project Deep Dive: Choose a recent project you know deeply and can walk through end-to-end from both a technical and business perspective. You will need to go over the goal, requirements, proposals, components, tradeoffs, timeline, and learnings. Be prepared to discuss architecture, measurable impact, and what you would improve if you revisited the project today.

2. Tenets Alignment: This will be a series of behavioral questions that will cover breaking down larger problems in a structured way, dealing with ambiguity, handling conflict, and evaluating tradeoffs.

Key tenets they’ll evaluate include:

* Customer focus
* Ownership
* Collaboration
* Bias for action
* Thoughtful tradeoffs
* First-principles thinking
* Continuous improvement

3. HM/Peer HM: This will go over examples of technical leadership, delivering impact, and applying feedback.

General Tips

* Use the CARL format: Challenge, Action, Result, plus key learnings.
* Be specific about your individual contributions.
* Share measurable impact where possible: performance, reliability, customer experience, cost, revenue, quality, etc.
* Be ready to explain tradeoffs, decisions, challenges, and what you would do differently.
* Keep answers concise, structured, and outcome-focused.

Please share at least 5 windows of availability for this week or next for 2.5hrs that work well for you. We’ll coordinate from there! If you're able to come on-site for this round to Aliso Viejo, please let us know. Otherwise, this round will be done over zoom.

Enter your availability now > ( https://s101.recruiting.eu.greenhouse.io/availability/92801f2db5427cfd3434da67a0c177b4?utm_medium=email&utm_source=AvailabilityRequest&utm_source=Automated )

We're looking forward to hearing from you. Once we match up the calendars we'll send a confirmation email with more details.

Best of luck in the final round!

Best,
Joseph
StubHub Talent Acquisition Team

lastPrompt: Hi can you read my email and update my lists. I submitted availability for rivian

content.text:
Updated through Tuesday evening (Oct 13). Big day: **StubHub moved you to the final round**, Rivian and CrowdStrike both advanced, and Aurora's system design is booked for tomorrow morning. Still 21 companies.

## On your side

1. **StubHub — submit availability for the final round.** Joseph wants at least five 2.5-hour windows this week or next, through the Greenhouse link. It is three 45-minute behavioral interviews: project deep dive, tenets alignment, and hiring manager. He also asks whether you can come on-site to Aliso Viejo; otherwise it runs over Zoom.
2. **Nubank — case study due tomorrow (Wed Oct 14)**, emailed to Alice Lobos.
3. **Zipline — panel presentation** for tomorrow at 1:30pm.
4. **Intuit — still unconfirmed.** You pinged Lakshmi at 5:12pm for the prep-and-confirmation call and she hasn't answered by email. Keep holding Thu Oct 15 12:30–2:00pm and Fri Oct 16 1:15–2:30pm.
5. **GitHub — sign the NDA** before the recruiter call, if you haven't. I can't see whether it's done.
6. **Audible hotel charge** — the reimbursement steps in Jaramie's Oct 12 email, if still outstanding.

Rivian is off your list: I've marked availability as submitted on your word, since the portal doesn't show up in email.

**Tomorrow is stacked:** Aurora system design at 9:30, Gusto at 1:00, Zipline from 1:30 to 5:00, and the Nubank deadline.

## Everything in flight (21)

All times ET.

| Company | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Aurora | Senior SWE, Full Stack | Virtual system design **Wed Oct 14 9:30–10:30am**; onsite done Oct 12 |
| Gusto | Staff SWE, Financial Platform | Recruiter screen **Wed Oct 14 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Zipline | Senior SWE, ASW Launch Ops | Virtual onsite **Wed Oct 14 1:30–5:00pm** |
| Nubank | Staff SWE | Case study due **Wed Oct 14**, then presentation |
| Duolingo | Senior/SWE II, Backend | Technical video interview **Thu Oct 15 10:30–11:30am** |
| Intuit | Staff level | Final round **Thu Oct 15 or Fri Oct 16**, awaiting confirmation |
| Tesla | Distributed Systems Engineer, Fintech | CoderPad interview **Thu Oct 15 2:00–2:45pm** |
| Stripe | Backend Engineer, Data & AI | Recruiter call **Thu Oct 15 4:15–4:45pm** |
| CoreWeave | Senior SWE I | Interview **Fri Oct 16 4:30–5:15pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Deploy at Scale | Team interviews **Tue Oct 20 2:00–5:00pm** and **Thu Oct 22 3:45–5:30pm** |
| Cloudflare | Senior SWE, Internal Fraud Platform | Team interviews **Thu Oct 22 9:00am–12:15pm** |
| Affirm | Staff SWE, Backend (Identity Decisioning) | Recruiter call **Mon Oct 26 1:00–1:30pm** |
| Riot Games | — | Phone screen **Tue Oct 27 3:00–3:30pm** |
| GitHub | Staff SWE, Git Systems | Recruiter call with Kevin Lamsback booked; the time is only in the calendar attachment, which I can't open |
| StubHub | Senior SWE, Supply Core | **Passed technical; final round** to be scheduled |
| Rivian | Staff SWE | **Passed recruiter screen**; 45-minute Zoom interview being scheduled |
| CrowdStrike | Back-end engineer, Identity | **Hiring manager wants to interview you**; she's at an offsite until Friday, update to follow |
| Klaviyo | Senior SWE, Platform Engineering | Hiring manager screen done today; awaiting result |
| Render | Software Engineer, Product | Technical screen done Oct 9; awaiting result |
| Robinhood | Senior SWE, Enterprise Build | Architecture interview done Oct 8; awaiting result |
| BrightHire | AI engineering | No reply from Will Decker since Oct 6 |

Long shot: **Chime** — nothing since Oct 8.

## Also in the mail

- **Gusto** rejected a different application (Staff SWE, Invoicing and Billing). Tomorrow's Financial Platform screen is still on; the reminder went out this afternoon.
- Application-stage rejections: Okta, Zillow, GitLab, Blue Origin, Salesforce (Principal Backend), Uber (Merchant Intel).

Updated as of Tuesday night (Oct 13). Three things landed since the last pass: **Salesforce is new**, **Intuit is confirmed for Thursday**, and **Rivian is booked**. That makes 22 companies.

## On you to schedule

Only one item:

1. **StubHub final round.** Joseph wants at least five 2.5-hour windows this week or next, through the Greenhouse link, plus a yes or no on coming on-site to Aliso Viejo (otherwise Zoom). I see no sign this has been submitted.

Everything else that needed a time now has one, or is waiting on the company.

## Other things on your side

- **Nubank case study** — due tomorrow (Wed Oct 14), emailed to Alice Lobos.
- **Release your Friday Intuit hold.** Shelby confirmed Thursday, so Fri Oct 16 1:15–2:30pm is free again.
- **GitHub NDA** — sign before the recruiter call, if you haven't.

## What changed

- **Intuit:** final round is **Thu Oct 15 3:00–4:15pm**. Shelby says a formal confirmation is coming. It ends exactly when Stripe starts at 4:15.
- **Rivian:** interview booked for **Tue Oct 20 9:00–9:30am**. Diana's email described it as 45 minutes, but the invite is 30.
- **Salesforce (new):** John McGinnes reached out about a GovCloud Distributed Systems Software Engineer role, and you booked a 15-minute intro for **Fri Oct 23 2:00–2:15pm**. The role requires US citizenship and is hybrid, at least one day a week at your nearest Salesforce office.

# Memory

- [Don't declare boards unscrapable](dont-declare-boards-unscrapable.md) — eight "impossible" careers boards, eight times wrong; exhaust the honest options first.
- [Dead links are jobwatch's recurring bug](jobwatch-dead-links-are-the-recurring-bug.md) — every user-reported bug has been a job link that didn't resolve.
- [Seed runs are jobwatch's fragile path](jobwatch-seed-runs-are-the-fragile-path.md) — a truncated seed corrupts quietly; test the seed, not the diff.
- [The role filter leaks unnamed disciplines](jobwatch-filter-leaks-unnamed-disciplines.md) — a denylist plus a "prefer keep" tiebreaker; fix the rule, not the instance.
- [Job search targeting criteria](job-search-targeting-criteria.md) — top comp plus household names; no quant firms; justify unfamiliar picks against the resume.
- [Levels.fyi access path](levels-fyi-access-path.md) — the `.md` routes robots.txt advertises; leaderboard is account-gated and pads with fake rows; WAF trips at ~400 fast requests.
- [Jobwatch productization plan](jobwatch-productization-plan.md) — turning the CLI into a multi-tenant alerts SaaS: Python→Postgres→Go→React, phased; Phase 0 done.
- [Jobwatch local run environment](jobwatch-local-run-environment.md) — use `.venv/bin/python3` + `source ~/.zshrc`; `tools/refilter_report.py` recovers a fail-open (unfiltered) run without re-scraping.
- [Jobwatch crash-before-report recovery](jobwatch-crash-before-report-recovery.md) — `tools/recover_interrupted_run.py` rebuilds a report from `state/` first_seen timestamps when a run died mid-scrape and never wrote to `output/` at all.
- [Jobwatch Anthropic credits keep running out](jobwatch-anthropic-credits-recurring-interruption.md) — six occurrences now (08-10, 19, 26, 30, 09-01, 09-22); when the outage outlasts the run, hand-filter with the filters.py prompt.
- [System design interview weak spot](system-design-interview-weak-spot.md) — recurring soft spot across Capital One, Datadog, and a Sept 2026 mock; the stall is the jump into high-level design.
- [Datadog system design prep](datadog-system-design-prep.md) — artifact walkthrough of an incident-investigation agent; request-path traversal + 45/30 DS-vs-AI rubric weighting.
- [Datadog code review round](datadog-code-review-round.md) — 60-min AI-enabled PR review; going with Go, run sheet artifact published.
- [Audible behavioral round](audible-behavioral-round.md) — 5 People Principles, not 6, and they do not replace the 16 LPs.
- [Capital One offer (Aug 2026)](capital-one-offer-2026-08.md) — Lead SWE Richmond, ~$210k total; declining, can't reach Devin's ~$330k bar.
- [Email-service deep-dive project](email-service-deep-dive-project.md) — Devin's reusable SNS→SQS P0 story; several facts still unconfirmed.
- [Plaid technical deep dive](plaid-technical-deep-dive.md) — 2×60-min first round; rubric adds prioritization and resourcing; deck in ~/Downloads.
- [Render pptx via PowerPoint](pptx-render-via-powerpoint.md) — no LibreOffice here; the group-container PDF export stopped working 2026-10-13, per-slide Quick Look thumbnails are the fallback.
- [Deep-dive decks follow story order](deep-dive-deck-story-order.md) — Devin's narrative order beats the template's; diagrams grow across build slides.
- [Relocation comp bar](relocation-comp-bar.md) — ~$365k NYC / ~$331k SF to match the Richmond life; supersedes the flat $330k for out-of-market roles.
- [Board moves need a re-seed](jobwatch-board-move-reseed.md) — ATS moves/re-IDs stick as suspicious forever; re-seed, then title-diff the old snapshot to recover the gap.
- [Chime Growth rejection](chime-growth-rejection.md) — 2026-09-25 "fit" rejection after strong loop; match the HM-round story to the team.
- [Seed-run blind spot](jobwatch-seed-blind-spot.md) — listings already up at first scrape never reach the digest; companies that keep listings up for months are invisible; page built 2026-09-27.
- [Expedia HM feedback (Sept 2026)](expedia-hm-feedback-2026-09.md) — itemized written feedback: gaps were producer-side capacity/priority design and production AI depth.
- [Inbox sweep method for the interview list](job-search-inbox-sweep-method.md) — four missed companies; never filter out recruiting-system senders, check starred, read every page.
- [Zipline onsite (Oct 2026)](zipline-onsite-2026-10.md) — 2026-10-14 virtual onsite; 45-min panel presentation to engineers and non-technical stakeholders, then stakeholder, architecture, culture rounds.
- [Slides: images over text](slides-prefer-images-over-text.md) — Devin wants icon-led slides with minimal text; he talks through the detail.
- [StubHub technical rounds](stubhub-technical-rounds.md) — Oct 8-9 2026 code pair + system design; reported questions are the "marketing engine" and an email notification system, not Ticketmaster.

This chat isn't in your claude.ai history because it's a Claude Code session, not a regular claude.ai chat. Claude Code sessions run on, and are saved to, the Mac you started them on: the transcript sits in `~/.claude/projects/` on this machine. Signing in elsewhere gives you your account, but not this machine's local sessions.

**To keep using this exact session from another device:**

- **Remote Control.** Your Mac keeps running the session, and you drive it from claude.ai/code or the Claude mobile app. This Mac has to stay on and awake. I can switch it on for you if you want.
- **Come back to this Mac.** The session is still in the Code tab sidebar here.

**To work from the other computer on its own:**

- **Start a fresh session there.** Connect Gmail and ask for the list. Nothing is lost on the email side, because I rebuild the list from your inbox each time.
- **What won't come along:** the notes I've saved about your search (sweep method, StubHub and Zipline prep, comp bar, and so on) and your jobwatch skip list. Both live only on this Mac.

content.text:
Your company list is already in git: `companies.txt` (267 companies) and the scraper registry in the code both came over with the push, so a clone on the other computer has them.

What's not in git is `state/`, which is jobwatch's database of what it has already seen:

- **268 per-company job snapshots.** These are how it knows which listings are new. Without them, the first run on the other computer is a fresh seed run, and you know that path is fragile.
- **Your skip list** (`skip_companies.txt`).
- **The filter cache** (10 MB) and the saved levels.fyi pages (7.5 MB).

It totals 82 MB. That's fine for a private repo, and no single file is anywhere near GitHub's limits.

**The catch is that it changes on every run.** Almost every snapshot file is rewritten each time, so committing it straight into jobwatch would bury your code history under thousands of data commits and grow the repo quickly.

**What I'd recommend:** a separate private repo, say `devinrhaslam/jobwatch-state`, checked out as the `state/` folder. The code repo stays clean, the database gets its own history, and on the other computer you clone both. Syncing after a run is a commit and push inside `state/`.

**The simpler alternative:** remove `state/` from `.gitignore` and commit it into jobwatch itself. One repo, but noisy history.

Which do you want? If it's the separate repo, I'll create it as private under devinrhaslam and push the current state. That creates a new repo on your account, so I'm checking before I do it.

content.text:
`state/` is now on GitHub inside jobwatch, in commit `e133be6`: all 2,620 files, including the snapshots, your skip list, the filter cache and the levels.fyi pages. I scanned it for keys and tokens first and found none. I also took `state/` out of `.gitignore`, and corrected the README line that said the skip list never gets committed.

On the other computer, the clone now brings the database along. After cloning and setting up the virtualenv, all you need to copy by hand is your API keys from `~/.zshrc`.

**Keeping the two computers in sync:** state doesn't sync on its own. Pull before running jobwatch on either machine, and push after:

```bash
git pull
```

```bash
git add state && git commit -m "Update state" && git push
```

If both machines run without syncing in between, the snapshot files will conflict. In that case, keep whichever side ran more recently.

`output/` (run reports) is still git-ignored, and `interview_prep/` is still uncommitted; say if you want either added.

structuredContent.plaintextBody:
Hi Devin,

Congratulations! We're excited to let you know that you've been selected to move forward in our interview process.

Your next step is a technical interview, conducted by Karat, a specialized third-party interviewing platform we've partnered with. Their trained interview engineers will evaluate your skills and share results with our team to inform the next steps in your process with Gusto. You should be receiving a separate email directly from Karat with a link to schedule your interview at a time that works best for you. Please keep an eye on your inbox (and spam folder, just in case!).

To help you prepare, I have attached two PDFs to this email that contains an overview of Karat, interview expectations, and interview prep information.

Don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions in the meantime.

Thank you!

Khetsun

content.text:
That's expected. Git only carries the files in the repo, and this chat was never one of them. Claude Code saves each session's transcript on the machine where it ran, under `~/.claude/projects/` on this Mac. So the clone brought jobwatch over but not our conversation.

**Ways to get the chat on the other computer:**

- **Remote Control (easiest).** This Mac keeps running the session and you continue it from the other computer through claude.ai/code. This Mac has to stay on and awake. I can turn it on for you.
- **Copy the transcript over.** The file is `~/.claude/projects/-Users-HMF4BGW-go-src-github-com-applications/4ca091e4-c518-4224-859c-dbbb11030c1a.jsonl`. Claude Code finds sessions by the project's folder path, so on the other computer it has to go into the projects folder whose name matches where you cloned jobwatch; then `claude --resume` in that folder should list it. I'm fairly confident this works in the terminal, less sure the desktop app's sidebar will show an imported session. Copy the `memory/` folder next to it at the same time so my notes on your search come along.
- **Start fresh.** A new session there can rebuild your interview list from Gmail, so nothing on the job-search side is lost.

**Don't put the transcript in git**, not even the private repo. It contains the Claude API key Intuit emailed you for the interview, your phone numbers, and the contents of a lot of recruiter email. Move it with AirDrop.

I can bundle the transcript and the `memory/` folder into one zip on your Desktop for AirDrop, or switch on Remote Control. Which do you want?

content.text:
I couldn't do it. Claude Code's automatic permission check blocked copying this session's transcript into git, because it holds credentials (the Intuit API key) and other sensitive email content. The block came before the command ran, so nothing was copied, committed or pushed, and your repo is as it was after the last push. It also blocked my follow-up `git status`, so I couldn't double-check that myself.

It's your data and your private repo, so it's your call. Two ways forward:

**Run it yourself** in [terminal tab 0](#terminal/0), from the jobwatch folder. Each command is its own block, in order.

Make the folder:

```bash
mkdir -p claude_session
```

Copy the transcript, its session folder, and my notes:

```bash
cp -R ~/.claude/projects/-Users-HMF4BGW-go-src-github-com-applications/4ca091e4-c518-4224-859c-dbbb11030c1a* ~/.claude/projects/-Users-HMF4BGW-go-src-github-com-applications/memory claude_session/
```

Commit and push:

```bash
git add claude_session && git commit -m "Add Claude Code session snapshot and notes" && git push
```

**Or allow it for me** by adding a permission rule for Bash in your Claude Code settings; after that, ask again and I'll do it.

**Restoring it on the other computer**, from the cloned jobwatch folder:

1. Make the matching projects folder:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.claude/projects/$(pwd | tr '/' '-')
   ```
2. Copy the session and notes into it:
   ```bash
   cp -R claude_session/* ~/.claude/projects/$(pwd | tr '/' '-')/
   ```
3. Open it:
   ```bash
   claude --resume
   ```

The copy is a snapshot as of now; anything after it stays only on this Mac.
